_comment: Single source of truth for everything the Tier B/C container packaging
profiles (apps/truenas, apps/unraid, apps/openmediavault, and any later
profile that wraps the same image) have to agree on. WP4.3's REFACTOR
step asks for exactly this: the three platforms' metadata is generated
from and checked against one file instead of drifting independently.
apps/common/packaging's test suite fails the build if any platform's
own metadata disagrees with a value in here.

note: published:false is the honest state, matching container/release-manifest.json's
own note: no registry is configured for this repository yet, so this reference
resolves to nothing today. It is the intended publish target and the one string
every provider package must carry, so that pointing the project at a real
registry is a one-line change here rather than an edit in four metadata formats.
Every acceptance procedure in docs/acceptance/ opens with a step 0 covering how
to make the image resolvable in the meantime (push to your own registry, or
docker save/load), and every profile keeps the reference substitutable.

truenas.hostPathNote: tank is the pool name the defaults assume; docs/acceptance/truenas-provider-acceptance.md step 0.2 covers substituting a real pool.

unraid.hostPathNote: appdata holds private state, the backups user share holds retained artifacts; §19.2 keeps those two separate security domains.

openmediavault.hostPathNote: dev-disk-by-uuid is a placeholder, deliberately matching what apps/openmediavault/frontend/platform.ts already declares: a real OMV system mounts data filesystems at /srv/dev-disk-by-uuid-<UUID>/, which differs per machine. The profile funnels every host path through one env file so the UUID is substituted exactly once.
